3h3ehk9gudrrgj856pti99r5vo: How much red, green and blue, each from 0 to 1.
257m154mfmiq7jci6usguldic2: How many steps of z → z · z + c it takes z to leave the circle of radius 2 (re² + im² past 4), from where it is; 300 when it hasn't by then. Those that never leave are the Mandelbrot set. z and c are Complex, so · is the complex product and + the complex sum: the same + and · as for any number.
pckrrp89t9rkvbbjc5s8b2r896: A colour for t, going round the hues as t grows: the circle of Ersagun's HSI at saturation 1/2, the largest circle that fits in the triangle of colours, at luminance 0.236, the brightest at which every hue on it can be shown. So every colour of the palette is equally bright.
6sdp5rnvo6f7nooifmclue40r3: The colour of the pixel at (x, y): the point c of the plane under it, in a picture zoom(time) wide around −0.7436 + 0.1318i in Seahorse Valley, where the set's edge curls into spirals. Black when it's in the Mandelbrot set, else a colour for how fast it escapes, shifting with time. escape counts its steps on a Float64, which the checker can't trust to stop (NaN + 1 is NaN), so with fuel allows 600 calls, twice what a pixel needs.
program:
Ersagun's: the colours are his HSI colour space, from his hsi-playground repository (a circle of hues at one luminance).
Prior art: the Mandelbrot set (Benoit Mandelbrot, 1980; drawn by counting escape steps, the standard method), zooming into Seahorse Valley near −0.7436 + 0.1318i, a classic place to zoom. Rec. 709's luminance weights and the sRGB transfer function are the standards.
Our own: written with the one + and · that every number type has, here at Complex, which the GPU runs as vec2f.
1e6qkbigpklqhador8pp7g0pbf: Ersagun's HSI (hue, saturation, intensity on linear RGB, from his hsi-playground): the colours of one intensity form a triangle with red, green and blue at its corners and gray at its centre. hue is in turns from red, saturation is 1 at the corners, and intensity is luminance with Rec. 709's weights, so two colours of one intensity are equally bright. Each channel is 1 + 2 · saturation · cos(the hue's angle from that channel's corner), scaled to the intensity.
ora59n0qt1b5q82p93us2hsaer: Linear light as the screen's value for it: the sRGB transfer function (IEC 61966-2-1).
qt6mottpu0m2jfu5k68um3v6tn: How wide a part of the plane the picture shows at a time: 3 wide, the whole set, at first, then in to 0.006 wide and back out, every 30 seconds. depth goes 0 to 1 and back, eased at the turns (smoothstep), and the width is 3 · 0.002^depth, so the zoom looks the same speed at every depth. Not 1 − cos: near 0 the GPU's cos is only good to about 0.0005, and 1 − cos would keep only that error. Deeper than 0.006 the GPU's 32-bit floats run out of digits.
